entities.name: Archelaus I of Macedon
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Archelaus I of Macedon (413–399 BC) was the capable and beneficent ruler of ancient Macedon, transforming the kingdom into a stronger power through sweeping changes in state administration, the military, and commerce. 

 Under his leadership, Macedon's military infrastructure was revamped, with Thucydides crediting Archelaus with doing more for his kingdom's military infrastructure than all of his predecessors together. 

 By the time of his death in 398 BCE, Archelaus had succeeded in converting Macedon into a significantly stronger power. 

 The impact of Archelaus's rule can still be felt in the modern world, with his legacy influencing the development of modern Greek politics and society.
